newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called $0.5-$1 higher, Brent up 8-15 c.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called $0.5-$1 higher, Brent up 8-15 c.

text.p: IPE May gas oil was called to open 50 cents to $1 a tonne higher on Wednesday while June Brent was called eight to 15 cents up, traders said.
"I am calling gas oil $0.5 to $1 higher on the back of what happened on the APIs," one broker said. "They were neutral to bullish APIs."

May gas oil settled $1.50 lower at $163.75 on Tuesday, dragged down by NYMEX, after having hit an intraday high of $167. Brent settled 35 cents down at $17.99 a barrel, shedding earlier gains as it was pressured by sharp falls in NYMEX crude.

The weekly inventory data issued by the American Petroleum Institute (API) late on Tuesday showed a 4.7 million barrel draw on distillates, defying market expectations of a half-million barrel decline. Heating oil shrank by 1.07 million barrels.
The data showed a gasoline draw of 1.9 million barrles for the week of April 19.

"The gasoline drawdown will give some support to the market. The heating oil drawdown was totally unexpected so that's why we see the slightly higher ACCESS move on the NYMEX Number Two (contract) overnight," one broker said.
Brent closed lower on Tuesday pressured by sharp falls in NYMEX crude on profit-taking ahead of the expiry of the May crude contract later that session.
June Brent broke through the $18 psychological support level in the final 10 minutes of trade. The close compared with an intra-day high of $18.64.
